After Hours Is a Passion Project Camper Van With Soft Blue Cabinetry and Trail-Ready Capability
23 photos
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Summit Vans Australia
Meet After Hours, a conversion based on a 2024 AWD Mercedes-Benz Sprinter with a 144" wheelbase. Why this name? Well, it was built by Shane from Summit Vans Australia as a personal project on his own time, after hours and during the weekends.
Summit Vans is a Wollongong, Australia-based company specializing in high-end camper van conversions. Shane was actually the first ever employee the two founders hired.
Since Shane worked on the van when he had spare time, it took him almost two years to complete the build. He designed it as a personal family adventure van. He had been using it for a couple of years. A few months ago, he listed it for sale, and it quickly made its way to the new owner shortly after.
You can definitely tell that this van was built by a professional. Before we take a more in-detail look at the interior, let's see what we can find on the outside.
The vehicle rides on Summit Vans wheels wrapped in all-terrain tires. Shane took things up a notch and, together with Summit Vans, they used this rig as a test mule for a new shock kit done in collaboration between Summit Vans and Bilstein Australia.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Summit Vans Australia Specifically, the van sports a Bilstein 5160 rear shock retuned to fit a Sprinter van, a GVM (Gross Vehicle Mass) upgraded rear leaf spring, Baja brackets, a front auxiliary shock, and a front Bilstein B60 strut replacement.
At the front, you'll come across a Weldbeat bull bar that continues into a skidplate underneath. On the opposite end, Shane fitted a spare tire carrier/ladder and a Flarespace snowboard rack.
Climb on top of the van, and you'll find a Wedgetail roof rack. It holds four front-facing Stedi light pods (two clear and two amber), a cargo box with an 80 W solar panel on top, Maxtrax traction boards, a Fiamma awning, a snowboard rack, and two 200 W solar panels. The roof also has cut-outs for two Maxxair vent fans.
Other notable mods include Weldbeat side steps, power and water hookups, and a set of flares. Flares, also known as pods or capsules, are designed to increase the van width to allow you to fit a bed inside in an east to west arrangement instead of the normal north to south.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Summit Vans Australia Stepping inside, you'll be greeted by a clean and functional interior. Regarding aesthetics, Shane opted for a slatted bamboo ceiling with recessed LED light strips, wall panels upholstered in grey woven vinyl fabric, soft blue laminated cabinetry, and grey woven vinyl flooring.
The interior has an open layout, with no wall separating the driver's cabin from the living space. In the top part of the cabin, you'll find a large headliner shelf with an L-Track that allows you to hang gear or set up a curtain to separate the two areas.
This open layout allowed for better use of the overall space. For instance, the front part of the interior was turned into a seating area. The driver and passenger seats are mounted on swivel bases, so they can be turned around to face the back of the van.
The seating area continues just a bit further back in the form of a double bench seat straight ahead as you enter.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Summit Vans Australia You'll notice a fold-down table in between the bench and the two cabin seats, attached to an L-Track integrated into the wall. Another L-Track higher up offers additional mounting points and holds a soft overhead cabinet.
Next, we have a kitchen on the passenger side, by the entrance. It features a deep black stainless steel sink with a cover, a 65-liter Bushman's fridge with a tiny freezer compartment, and a portable induction stove.
A pull-out pantry and two drawers are available for storage. There's also an overhead cabinet that hides the "command center" for the rig's utilities. It includes a variety of light switches, some of which are dimmer switches, as well as a battery monitor and a timer switch for the water heater.
Shane even found the space to devise one of the most sought-after facilities in camper vans: a bathroom. It sits opposite the kitchen and offers a shower with a handheld wand and a toilet. Moreover, a roll-down door prevents any water from splashing outside.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Summit Vans Australia The bathroom can also double as a drying room. It has a vent connected to a diesel heater that pumps hot air and a wall-mounted L-Track that you can use to hang your clothes and gear.
Your bulkiest items are meant to go on the largest storage area inside this van: the garage underneath the bedroom, which is accessible from both inside and outside the van.
The garage offers heaps of storage space in the middle, and makes accessing your items easier thanks to a pull-out tray. Furthermore, on the sides, there are two black hex-ply boxes that accommodate the utility systems.
Power is on the left side – the electrical heart is a Bluetti AC240P portable power station . It has a 2,400 W AC output and a 1,843 Wh capacity and stays topped up thanks to three charging sources: solar power, shore power, and DC-DC charging.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Summit Vans Australia On plumbing, the van is equipped with two water tanks (one for fresh water and the other for grey water), an outdoor shower connection, and a Dieselheat DH9 hydronic heater. The latter provides both heated air and hot water.
All in all, it's obvious that Shane put a ton of work into his After Hours build. Not only does it pack so many creature comforts and offers abundant storage space, but it also has a welcoming, home-like design.
